name: Isometric Projection
description: Maps tile coordinates to screen pixels and back. The forward half is the three lines everybody writes; the inverse is the half that gets skipped, and skipping it is why an isometric prototype can draw a world it cannot tell you the mouse is over. Both directions are declared here so they can be held to being exact inverses of each other. `zoom` is a declared INPUT and was only ever read once, at construction, which makes it a number a request sets and a player cannot. Zooming a map is not a rebuild — the world does not change, the lens does — so `setZoom` is published beside it: same number, same clamp, changed live. The origin re-fits on the next frame because it is derived from the viewport and the board rather than declared, which is exactly why it was never an input.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application (generator/iso/IsoProjection.ts); not verifiable from this repository.
A 3D camera does its own projection.

inputs.name: tileWidth
inputs.description: Screen width of one tile diamond, in pixels.

inputs.name: tileHeight
inputs.description: Screen height of one tile diamond. The 2:1 ratio against tileWidth is what makes the grid read as isometric rather than merely rotated.

inputs.name: elevationPixels
inputs.description: Pixels one elevation level lifts a tile up the screen.

inputs.name: spriteScale
inputs.description: How big a standing sprite is ON SCREEN, in screen pixels per art pixel, for everything that stands on a tile: characters, pillars, chests, loot. 0 means the painter's own rule (one integer step per fourteen pixels of tile). Set, it is divided by the camera's zoom so the number a request writes is the number a player sees — a build at camera zoom 2 asking for 3 draws its bodies at one and a half world pixels per art pixel, which is three on screen. The floor and wall tiles are not touched: a body can stand three-quarters the height of a wall block without the wall shrinking with it, which is the difference between a figure in a room and a figure in a dollhouse.

outputs.name: setZoom
outputs.description: Set the zoom live, clamped to the same range the input is. It exists because a lens is not a level: changing how close you are looking should not tear down the world and rebuild it, and a rebuild is what a change to a declared input means everywhere else.

outputs.name: zoom
outputs.description: The current zoom, which after setZoom is not necessarily the one the request asked for. Published so a control can show where it actually is rather than what it last requested.
